$comment: The fleet's plan of record. FLEET.md is generated from this; edit here. Held by scripts/check-fleet.mjs, which verifies each claimed tier against the repository rather than taking the entry's word for it.

tiers.0: Has not adopted. The gate is off in its workflow.
tiers.1: Drift check, tracked-artifacts check, backlog, shared rules.
tiers.2: Tier 1 plus an executed-count assertion wired to a real test report.
tiers.3: Tier 2 plus mutation canaries against its own gates, and the Bugbot verdict job.

$onlineComment: When the tier claims below were last checked against the repositories themselves, rather than only read back off this file. Null means never. The offline run — the only one a pull request can perform, since its token cannot see a private sibling — warns until onlineGraceUntil and fails after it. Deferral is fine; undated deferral becomes permanent by accident, and this file's whole purpose is to not become fiction.

projects.note: Origin of the kit. Keeps its own bespoke contracts alongside the shared ones; becomes a consumer of the shared copies rather than keeping duplicates.
projects.evidenceReason: Consumes the vendored kit at the canonical paths since #191. Two artefacts stay bespoke: the backlog is a typed TS registry rather than JSON because its tests type-check the entries, and the canary list is keyed to this repo own gates.

projects.note: Tier 3 pilot, adopted in #60. Playwright across four shards with its own e2e spec registry, mutation canaries, and the Bugbot verdict job. Does not call the shared browser-compat workflow — it runs a sharded e2e job of its own, which is why the fleet-wide browser-compat default only silently truncated other repositories' suites.

Tier 2 pilot, adopted in #39. The awkward case: the build is Make plus Python plus esbuild and `npm test` is a placeholder that exits 1. Proves the kit works when the runner is not npm. Carries an open confirmed bug — its anti-spam submit floor fails intermittently after a prerender.
Tier 1 pilot, adopted in #3. No package.json, no tests, 49 files. Proves the floor: if the kit needs npm here, the design is wrong. Publish-set verification inverted to an extension allow-list.

No test suite, so tier 1 is its ceiling until it has one. Its publish-set check found two files live on the public site that were never meant to be served — nginx-routes.conf and LICENSE — within seconds of being written. Removing them needs a deploy, not just the .deployignore commit.
No test suite, so tier 1 is its ceiling. Publish-set verification inverted to an extension allow-list.
Executed-count floor wired through the shared browser-compat job.

Its whole accessibility suite — axe scans, skip link, keyboard focus, contrast — had never run in CI, because browser-compat defaulted to naming one spec file. Carries an open confirmed bug: production answers on four URLs per page, with client-side redirects where server-side 301s are asserted.

Its security audit had never executed once: the npm script invoked the wrong interpreter, and `npm audit` was suppressed with `|| true`. Behind it, 32 advisories including 8 critical, and zero security headers served in production — both open in its backlog.
No test suite, so tier 1 is its ceiling. The one site already immune to the deny-list publishing defect, because it stages an allow-list into a clean directory and ships that.

Sixteen cross-browser tests were failing and had been merged over. Cause was its own meta CSP, not a browser: `upgrade-insecure-requests` in a meta element broke the http preview server. Serves zero security headers in production — `_headers` is a Netlify convention and the site is on Cloudflare — and `frame-ancestors` is ignored in a meta element, so it is framable. Both open in its backlog.

Tier 1 rather than 2 on purpose. Its 49 tests do have an executed-count floor, but pytest emits neither a Playwright nor a Vitest JSON report, so the floor lives in a pytest_collection_modifyitems hook in tests/conftest.py rather than in the shared assertion. Claiming tier 2 would describe a wiring that is not there. First repository to need rule-sources scoped, because it vendors a bundled AngularJS.

Executed-count floor wired through browser-compat. Its unit suite needed a second, local floor: `node --test` with a shell glob exits 0 when the glob matches nothing, and that suite is one of only two gates on a pull request. No production monitor exists here at all — open in its backlog.
Holds the canonical kit. Gated harder than the copies, because a template defect replicates fourteen times.
projects.evidenceReason: This is the source, not a consumer: the kit lives under templates/ and is not vendored into itself. Only the kit paths move; its backlog is at the standard location.

tierTwoFloor.reason: This repository is the kit rather than a consumer of it, so it has no shared-workflow caller to pass test-report through. Its executed-count floor is the inline comparison on its own kit suite, and the pattern above is verified in the named workflow rather than taken on trust.
